stories.headline: Anthropic Leak Reveals Claude Mythos, a 'Step Change' Model With Major Cybersecurity Capabilities

key_facts.fact: A CMS misconfiguration exposed draft blog posts about an unreleased model called Claude Mythos (also codenamed Capybara) in a publicly accessible data store.
key_facts.excerpt: A draft blog post and structured data for an unreleased AI model were discovered in an unsecured, publicly accessible data cache.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic confirmed the model is real, calling it 'the most capable we've built to date' and 'a step change' in AI performance.
key_facts.excerpt: An Anthropic spokesperson characterized it as representing 'a step change' in AI performance and 'the most capable we've built to date.'

key_facts.fact: Mythos is described as a new tier of model, larger and more intelligent than Opus, with 'dramatically higher scores' in coding, academic reasoning, and cybersecurity.
key_facts.excerpt: Capybara gets dramatically higher scores on tests of software coding, academic reasoning, and cybersecurity, among others.

key_facts.fact: The leaked documents describe the model as 'currently far ahead of any other AI model in cyber capabilities,' warning it 'presages an upcoming wave of models that can exploit vulnerabilities in ways that far outpace the efforts of defenders.'
key_facts.excerpt: Currently far ahead of any other AI model in cyber capabilities... presages an upcoming wave of models that can exploit vulnerabilities in ways that far outpace the efforts of defenders.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic plans a phased rollout, starting with early access for organizations to evaluate cybersecurity applications before broader API availability.
key_facts.excerpt: Access begins with early-access customers focused on evaluating cybersecurity applications, then gradually expands through the Claude API.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic acknowledged the model is 'very expensive for us to serve, and will be very expensive for our customers to use' and plans optimization before broader release.
key_facts.excerpt: The company acknowledged the model is 'very expensive for us to serve, and will be very expensive for our customers to use' and plans optimization before broader release.

stories.headline: Google's TurboQuant Algorithm Compresses AI Memory 6x, Wipes ~$100B From Memory Chip Stocks

key_facts.fact: Google Research published TurboQuant, a two-stage compression algorithm (PolarQuant + Quantized Johnson-Lindenstrauss) that reduces LLM inference KV cache memory by at least 6x with no accuracy loss.
key_facts.excerpt: TurboQuant is a compression algorithm that reduces the memory footprint of large language models during inference... At least 6x smaller KV cache footprint.

key_facts.fact: The algorithm achieves 3-bit precision compression and up to 8x faster attention operations on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, requiring no model retraining.
key_facts.excerpt: Up to 8x faster attention operations on NVIDIA H100 GPU (4-bit vs. 32-bit). Down to 3-bit precision with no accuracy loss on tested benchmarks. No retraining required for existing models.

key_facts.fact: US memory chip stocks fell sharply: SanDisk (-6.5%), Seagate (-5%), Micron (-4%), Western Digital (-4%); in Asia, SK Hynix fell 4.42% and Samsung 3.02%.
key_facts.excerpt: SanDisk (-6.5%), Micron Technology (-4%), Western Digital (-4%), Seagate (-5%). SK Hynix (-4.42%), Samsung Electronics (-3.02%).

key_facts.fact: US memory chip stocks lost approximately $100 billion in market value during the week, led by Micron's 15% weekly drop.
key_facts.excerpt: US memory chip stocks lost ~$100B in market value this week, led by Micron's 15% drop, after Google Research detailed its TurboQuant compression algorithm.

key_facts.fact: The paper is slated for presentation at ICLR 2026. Analysts invoked the Jevons Paradox, suggesting efficiency gains could increase total AI memory demand through wider adoption.
key_facts.excerpt: Slated for presentation at ICLR 2026. Analysts invoked the 'Jevons Paradox' suggesting efficiency gains could actually increase total demand.

stories.headline: NeurIPS Reverses Sanctions Ban on Chinese Researchers After Boycott Threat From CCF and CAST

key_facts.fact: On March 23, NeurIPS updated its handbook to ban submissions, peer review, and publication from anyone linked to US-sanctioned organizations including Huawei, SMIC, and SenseTime.
key_facts.excerpt: On March 23, 2026, NeurIPS updated its handbook requiring compliance with US sanctions laws, stating that 'no services — including paper submissions, peer review, or publication' would be available to anyone linked to sanctioned organizations.

key_facts.fact: China Computer Federation (CCF) urged all Chinese researchers to boycott NeurIPS, and China Association for Science and Technology (CAST) halted funding and said NeurIPS papers would no longer count toward academic evaluations in China.
key_facts.excerpt: CCF urged all Chinese researchers to boycott NeurIPS. CAST halted funding for researchers attending the 2026 event and announced NeurIPS papers would no longer count toward academic evaluations or promotions in China.

key_facts.fact: On March 27, NeurIPS reversed the policy and apologized, admitting it had 'gone beyond legal requirements' and the handbook 'pointed to a broad US sanctions tool that covered more restrictions than actually needed.'
key_facts.excerpt: NeurIPS issued an apology, admitting they had 'gone beyond legal requirements' and that the handbook 'pointed to a broad US sanctions tool that covered more restrictions than actually needed.'

key_facts.fact: The corrected policy now applies only to entities on the US Treasury's SDN (Specially Designated Nationals) list rather than the broader sanctions list.
key_facts.excerpt: The policy was a mistake due to a miscommunication with their legal team and clarified that it applies only to entities on the U.S. Treasury's SDN list.

stories.headline: Coinbase and Better launch first crypto-backed conforming mortgage with Fannie Mae backing

key_facts.fact: Better and Coinbase launched the first token-backed conforming mortgage in the US, allowing borrowers to pledge Bitcoin or USDC as collateral for their down payment instead of liquidating crypto holdings.
key_facts.excerpt: Prospective homebuyers will be able to use the Bitcoin or USDC in their Coinbase accounts to fund their cash down payments.

key_facts.fact: The product creates two loans at closing: a standard Fannie Mae conforming mortgage on the home, and a second loan secured by pledged crypto that funds the down payment. Both share the same interest rate and amortization term with one combined monthly payment.
key_facts.excerpt: You get two loans at closing. The first is a standard Fannie Mae mortgage on the home. The second is used to fund your cash down payment, and is secured by the crypto that you pledge.

key_facts.fact: Interest rates for the crypto-backed mortgages will be 0.5 to 1.5 percentage points higher than a standard 30-year mortgage, depending on the consumer profile.
key_facts.excerpt: The rates for the crypto-backed mortgages will be higher than a standard 30-year by between half a percentage point and 1.5 percentage points.

key_facts.fact: The token-backed mortgages are free of margin calls and top-ups. If BTC drops in value, mortgage terms remain unchanged and no additional collateral is required. Liquidation of collateral is only triggered by a 60-day payment delinquency, not by market movements.
key_facts.excerpt: Token-backed mortgages would be free of margin calls and top-ups. Market movements alone never trigger liquidation. Borrowers' collateral is at risk of liquidation only in the event of a 60-day payment delinquency.

key_facts.fact: Coinbase One members approved for a loan by Better will be eligible for up to $10,000 in closing cost credits.
key_facts.excerpt: Coinbase One members will be eligible for up to $10,000 in closing cost credits.

key_facts.fact: The product aims to expand homeownership access to approximately 52 million Americans who hold crypto but previously could not get credit for those assets in mortgage underwriting without liquidating and potentially triggering capital gains taxes.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies aim to expand homeownership access to approximately 52 million Americans.

stories.headline: Stripe launches Projects, a CLI tool that lets AI agents provision services and manage credentials

key_facts.fact: Stripe launched Projects, a CLI tool that lets developers and AI coding agents provision services, generate and store credentials, and manage billing from the terminal, eliminating manual dashboard sign-ups.
key_facts.excerpt: We decided to build Stripe Projects to help agents instantly provision services from the CLI.

key_facts.fact: A single command like 'stripe projects add posthog/analytics' creates a PostHog account, gets an API key, and sets up billing automatically.
key_facts.excerpt: Simply run: $ stripe projects add posthog/analytics. And it'll create a PostHog account, get an API key, and (as needed) set up billing.

key_facts.fact: Patrick Collison framed the tool as solving the problem Andrej Karpathy identified when building MenuGen: that vibe-coding apps is fun but deploying them requires manually assembling accounts, API keys, and configurations across many services.
key_facts.excerpt: Building a modern app is a bit like assembling IKEA furniture. There are all these services, docs, API keys, configurations, dev/prod deployments.

key_facts.fact: Launch partners include hosting (Vercel, Railway), databases (Neon PostgreSQL, Supabase, Turso, PlanetScale, Chroma), auth (Clerk), analytics (PostHog), and sandbox (Runloop), with more providers coming.
key_facts.excerpt: Hosting (Vercel, Railway), databases (Neon PostgreSQL, Supabase, Turso, PlanetScale, Chroma), auth (Clerk), analytics (PostHog), and sandbox (Runloop).

key_facts.fact: Credentials are automatically generated, synced to environment variables, and changes remain auditable and repeatable. CLI commands include 'stripe projects init', 'stripe projects catalog', 'stripe projects add', and 'stripe projects upgrade'.
key_facts.excerpt: Credentials are automatically generated, synced to environment variables, and changes remain auditable and repeatable.

key_facts.fact: Stripe Projects is launching as a developer preview with open registration at projects.dev, with plans to make it available to everyone soon.
key_facts.excerpt: Projects is launching today as a developer preview. You can register for access (we'll make it available to everyone soon).
